objects.description: A standard library pair of two Eigen::MatrixXd objects used by readArray to return lidar and camera point arrays. This is a referenced standard template instantiation and not custom-defined here; included only for clarity. No custom definition exists in this header.
Eigen quaternion with double precision. Used for accumulating rotations. This is defined by Eigen, not in this header; no custom type is defined here.

functions.name: addQ
functions.description: Accumulates two quaternions with hemisphere correction. If the dot product a·b is negative, b is flipped (negated) to avoid averaging antipodal quaternions, then the components are added elementwise. Intended for incremental averaging/accumulation of rotations before normalization by the caller.
requirements: Inputs a and b should represent valid rotations (unit quaternions) for meaningful results; function does not normalize the sum.
Caller must normalize the returned quaternion if a rotation quaternion is required.
No side effects beyond returning the sum; parameters are passed by value.

functions.name: readArray
functions.description: Reads paired 3D point sets from file "<pkg_loc>/conf/points.txt" and returns them as two 3×N matrices (lidar, camera). The file is expected to contain: first an integer N (>0), then N lines of LiDAR points (x y z), followed by N lines of camera points (x y z). Note: a comment in code indicates a possible swap between lidar and camera storage; the function currently returns (lidar, camera).
requirements: ROS must be initialized and ros::package::getPath("lidar_camera_calibration") must succeed to resolve pkg_loc.
File "<pkg_loc>/conf/points.txt" must exist and be readable.
First token in the file must be an integer num_points > 0 (enforced by ROS_ASSERT).
The file must contain exactly 3*num_points doubles for lidar, followed by 3*num_points doubles for camera.
All numeric values should be finite; no handling for NaN/Inf is present.
Returns matrices of size 3×num_points.

functions.name: calc_RT
functions.signature: Eigen::Matrix4d calc_RT(Eigen::MatrixXd lidar, Eigen::MatrixXd camera, int MAX_ITERS, Eigen::Matrix3d lidarToCamera)
functions.description: Computes a rigid-body transform (rotation R and translation t) that best aligns LiDAR points to camera points using SVD (Umeyama/Kabsch-style) and returns a 4×4 homogeneous transform T where camera ≈ R·lidar + t. Also accumulates running averages across calls using module-level globals (translation_sum, rotation_sum, rotation_avg_by_mult, rmse_avg, iteration_counter) and logs intermediate/average values to "<pkg_loc>/log/avg_values.txt". Parameter MAX_ITERS is accepted but not used to iterate within this function; averaging evolves over repeated calls. lidarToCamera is only used for reporting a derived final_rotation in logs.
requirements: Inputs lidar and camera must both be 3×N with the same N and N > 0; columns correspond to matched point pairs.
Matrices should contain finite numeric values; no explicit checks exist for NaN/Inf.
Function relies on global state for averaging and logging; repeated calls increment a global iteration_counter and update running averages.
ROS package path pkg_loc must resolve and the log directory "<pkg_loc>/log" must exist and be writable to append avg_values.txt.
If the initial call (iteration_counter==0), the function truncates "avg_values.txt" and resets global accumulators.
The computed rotation is forced to be a proper rotation (determinant +1) by possibly flipping the last singular value.
Return is a 4×4 Matrix4d with top-left 3×3 rotation and top-right 3×1 translation.
MAX_ITERS has no effect on computation inside this function.
lidarToCamera is used only for computing a reported final_rotation; not used in T.

functions.name: readArucoPose
functions.description: Parses a flat marker_info array describing multiple marker poses and appends transformed board corner points to "<pkg_loc>/conf/points.txt". Each marker uses 7 floats: [marker_id, tx, ty, tz, rx, ry, rz], where r is a rotation vector (axis×angle in radians). For each marker, a 4×4 pose matrix is built from the rotation vector and translation, then per-marker board geometry from "<pkg_loc>/conf/marker_coordinates.txt" is transformed into marker/world coordinates and four 3D points are appended to points.txt.
requirements: ROS must be initialized and ros::package::getPath("lidar_camera_calibration") must succeed to resolve pkg_loc.
ROS_ASSERT enforces marker_info.size()/7 == num_of_marker_in_config; caller must satisfy this.
Each 7-float block must be ordered: marker_id (int convertible), translation (tx,ty,tz), rotation vector (rx,ry,rz).
Rotation vector must have non-zero norm; otherwise division by zero occurs when normalizing (rot/rot.norm()).
File "<pkg_loc>/conf/marker_coordinates.txt" must exist and be readable. Its first token is an integer num_of_markers, followed by num_of_markers lines each with 5 floats defining board parameters.

The function assumes num_of_markers <= marker_info.size()/7 since it indexes marker_pose[i] for i in [0, num_of_markers). Caller/config must ensure at least as many marker poses are provided as markers described in the file.
Outputs are appended to "<pkg_loc>/conf/points.txt"; the directory must exist and be writable.
All numeric inputs should be finite; no handling for NaN/Inf is present.

functions.name: find_transformation
functions.signature: void find_transformation(std::vector<float> marker_info, int num_of_marker_in_config, int MAX_ITERS, Eigen::Matrix3d lidarToCamera)
functions.description: High-level helper that generates point correspondences from marker poses and board definitions, reads them back, and computes a LiDAR-to-camera transform. It calls readArucoPose(marker_info,...), then readArray() to load 3×N point sets, and finally calc_RT(...) to compute a 4×4 transform. The returned transform from calc_RT is computed but not used or returned by this function.
requirements: All requirements of readArucoPose apply (marker_info formatting, files, writable points.txt, rotation vector norm > 0).
All requirements of readArray apply (points.txt format and existence).
All requirements of calc_RT apply (3×N matched point sets, logging path).
MAX_ITERS is passed through to calc_RT but has no effect there; no iteration within this function.
lidarToCamera is passed through to calc_RT for logging-derived final_rotation; not used otherwise.
